Maintenance Report — MNT-0101-001

Asset: WELL-0101 (NE-07 Well 101, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 21 Oct 2022 08:00 · Finished: 02 Nov 2022 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 292 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0101-0001 on 2022-10-20 Report written: 03 Nov 2022

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0101-0001 showed the wellhead at 23.1 °C with the air at 17.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0101-001 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0101-006

Asset: WELL-0101 (NE-07 Well 101, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 16 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 19 Jul 2023 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 75 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0101-0038 on 2023-07-13 Report written: 25 Jul 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0101-0038 showed the wellhead at 34.5 °C with the air at 33.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

The weekly drone inspection INS-0101-0053 at 13:00 on 2023-11-02 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.4% of the pad area, estimated 1.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

maintenance.action: Fished and replaced parted rod section
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0101-023

Asset: WELL-0101 (NE-07 Well 101, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: rod string Work started: 03 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 19 Aug 2025 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 377 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0101-0142 on 2025-07-31 Report written: 20 Aug 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0101-0142 showed the wellhead at 36.7 °C with the air at 36.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 14 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Rod couplings1,105
Fishing tool rental1,842
Labour (company crew and contractor)6,881
Total14,249

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.
